Inter Miami drew 2-2 in its match with Austin FC Saturday. It was the team's first match at the Nu Stadium in Miami's Freedom Park. Inter Miami signed a deal with Brazilian financial services company Nu, which will have the naming rights for the team's new stadium located in Miami Freedom Park. Nu Stadium, a 26,700-seat facility, plays host to its first match on April 4 and is seen as the centerpiece of the Freedom Park entertainment district that includes retail, dining, office spaces and hotel rooms. Following along for updates on the game and fan reactions. Lionel Messi scored on the long-awaited opening night in his new home stadium. And Luis Suarez found a way to tie things up late in the second half. It was good enough to salvage a point for Inter Miami. Messi scored on a header in the 10th minute, Suarez hammered home a volley in the 82nd minute and Inter Miami escaped with a 2-2 tie against Austin FC in the defending MLS champions' first match at their still-under-construction stadium near Miami International Airport on Saturday night. (Photo by Tomas Diniz Santos/Getty Images) Inter Miami (3-1-2) is now unbeaten in its last five MLS matches, and Austin (1-2-3) is now winless in its last four contests. It's a big moment for South Florida soccer on Saturday as Inter Miami is set to play its first match in its brand-new stadium in Miami's Freedom Park. Inter Miami signed a deal with Brazilian financial services company Nu, which will have the naming rights for the team's new stadium located in Miami Freedom Park. For many fans, it’s a moment they’ve been waiting years for, and the wait is finally over after years of planning, building and anticipation. "This is a stadium that was born out of a dream six years ago," said Jorge Mas, Inter Miami managing owner. "We didn’t have a club for us its important, and it was always our dream to build a special football stadium." Read Full ArticleDrama at NU stadium in this the 11th hour, before game night. The city and the team are still working to secure a temporary certificate of occupancy. NBC6’s Steve Litz reports Miami Police are warning drivers to plan ahead due to "major delays" around Nu Stadium before and after Inter Miami's match on Saturday. They advised the most congested traffic times will be before the match from 4 p.m. to 8 p.m., and post-match from 9:30 p.m. to 11:30 p.m. Miami International Airport officials are also advising travelers and visitors to plan and allow extra time due to the traffic around the stadium.
